chapter: Looking back, big bands and sidemen
title: Baritone players: Serge Chaloff, Hipner, Johnson, Smulyan
summary: Frank Hipner was a strange but outstanding player now in Reno; Bruce Johnson is outstanding, and Gary Smulyan from Long Island is a brilliant current player.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Let's see. How about Serge Chaloff? I know we're going back to these key figures.
Well, I think he was one of the earlier swinging jazz baritone saxophonists. A very loose and free
spirit in every direction, and that kind of player. He was heavily influenced by the early bop music, and he played baritone somewhat like Charlie Parker played alto. It was that --
Are there other outstanding baritone players in your band? I know you had Tommy Anastasis and Frank Hipner and people like that.
Yeah, Hipner was a very -- truly outstanding jazz player, but he was a kind of a strange young man, and he still resides, I think, in Reno.
Oh, does he?
Yeah.
I haven't heard about him for a long time.
And he works in a restaurant or something.
Really?
Yeah.
Oh, I thought he was a complement to the band.
Oh, yes, great player and I've had some really excellent baritone saxophonists in recent years, too.
Bruce Johnson.
Bruce Johnson, I think, is truly outstanding, and then currently I have a young man that I think is -- touches a brilliancy.
Oh, yes? What's his name?
His name is Gary Semolian.
Oh, yes.
And he's from Long Island area, actually, or Westchester. Several other players are from that place, and played in different school bands and different road-shop workshop bands in that area.
Uh-huh. I was thinking about something when you said upstate New York and so forth --
